death.note: doxologia.ro dates the events and not the man: Licinius reigned «(307-321)», Constantine took the Eastern empire from him «(324)», Paul was called to Nicaea «în anul următor», and after the Council «s-a întors în eparhia sa, unde s-a mai ostenit vreme de câțiva ani, apoi și-a dat cu pace sufletul». The year after 324 is the page's own arithmetic; the upper bound is left open because the page gives none.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 23 decembrie — «Sfântul Ierarh Pavel, Arhiepiscopul Neocezareei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 23ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Παύλος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Νεοκαισαρείας»

attestations.note: The life page `/3312/` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps for the Romanian, and it is the same man: the bishop whose hands Licinius had burned with red-hot irons and who showed the wounds at Nicaea. The listing calls him archbishop and the life page «επίσκοπος Νεοκαισάρειας», which is the same see the folder's `office` already names. **No `dates` key is drafted**: saint.gr gives the reign as «(307 - 323 μ.Χ.)» and then only «μετά από λίγα χρόνια απεβίωσε ειρηνικά», which is no more precise than the folder's own «after 325». It names the fortress of his exile only as one near the river Euphrates, and no coordinate is proposed. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (28 September 2026).
